subject: humanities
passage: In Japan during the Edo period (1603–1868), color woodblock prints were made by teams of artists and craftspeople. In the usual method, a carver cut a separate wooden block for each color in a design. A printer then pressed each block onto the same sheet of paper, one color at a time, lining up every block carefully. Under this method, a print that used ten colors would have required ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: fewer carved blocks than a print that used three colors.
choices.B: more carved blocks than a print that used three colors.
choices.C: one carved block holding all ten colors at the same time.
choices.D: a carver who had also designed the picture being printed.

explanation.why: The text says each color had its own block. A ten-color print therefore needed ten blocks, which is more than the three blocks a three-color print needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the relationship: more colors means more blocks, not fewer.
explanation.B: Correct. One block per color means ten blocks for ten colors, more than a three-color print needed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says a separate block was cut for each color, not one block for all of them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes teams of workers but never says carvers designed the pictures.
